profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting in an ML research lab that is trying to reproduce a paper result on tangent-space gradient optimization (TSGO) for a matrix-product-state Born machine. Their current implementation trains without immediate crashes, but on the lab's Fashion-MNIST 8x8 pooled benchmark the negative log-likelihood oscillates and TSGO does not outperform Adam as the paper claims. The agenda is to diagnose whether the problem comes from the update geometry, the normalization/canonicalization routine, or an apples-to-oranges comparison against the existing Adam baseline. The expected outcome is agreement on the most plausible root cause and a concrete debugging plan for the next experiment run.

members.name: Dr. Lina Zhou
members.role: Postdoctoral Researcher leading the reproduction study
members.expertise: Tensor networks for probabilistic modeling, optimization geometry, variational methods
members.background: Lina came from a physics-ML group and has been adapting tensor-network training methods from quantum many-body literature into the lab's generative modeling codebase.
members.private_state: She wants to preserve the core TSGO idea from the paper and is hoping the issue is an implementation detail rather than evidence that the method fails on the lab's benchmark; she is also trying to avoid a week-long rewrite of the update routine before an internal results review.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the MPS is 'normalized,' global wavefunction norm equal to 1 is the essential condition; restoring full canonical/isometric gauges after every step is mostly a numerical convenience.
A tangent-space update can be treated locally at the current optimization center tensor because mixed-canonical form already encodes the geometry around that site.
Referring to 'the Adam baseline' means the benchmark run listed in the reproduction spreadsheet, even if some implementation details changed across commits.
If the training no longer shows norm drift or NaNs in the first few epochs, the instability is effectively fixed and larger-scale reproduction issues can be addressed later.

members.name: Marco Alvarez
members.role: Research Engineer maintaining the tensor-network training stack
members.expertise: Numerical ML systems, experiment tracking, efficient MPS training pipelines, reproducibility tooling
members.background: Marco built the lab's MPS training infrastructure, including canonicalization sweeps, dataloaders, and experiment tracking; he is less attached to the paper's framing and more focused on whether the implementation matches the lab's operational conventions.
members.private_state: He wants a fix that produces a reproducible long-run training curve in the shared infrastructure, not just a theoretically correct local update; he is also worried that the team may be comparing against a stale Adam reference without noticing.
hidden_assumptions: In this codebase, saying the state is 'normalized' implicitly includes restoring the canonical center and isometric gauges, because downstream contractions assume that form.
A true tangent-space rotation for this model requires re-centering and re-projecting as the sweep moves, not just rotating a single active tensor with one local projector.
When someone mentions 'the Adam baseline,' they mean the latest tracked reference run in W&B after the minibatch-loss bug was fixed, not the older spreadsheet number.
A troubleshooting fix only counts if the full 20-epoch run is stable and the comparison curve is trustworthy enough to support a method claim.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree the state should be 'normalized after each update.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means rescaling so the global MPS wavefunction has norm 1, without necessarily restoring full mixed-canonical form immediately.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a normalization step that also re-canonicalizes the chain and re-establishes the orthogonality center expected by the training code.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In tensor-network work, 'normalization' often travels together with canonicalization, so both hear a familiar phrase and assume the same operational meaning without spelling out the exact routine.

misalignment_points.topic: How the tangent-space rotation is actually executed
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say they should 'project to the tangent space and rotate toward the gradient.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this can be implemented as a local update on the current center tensor using the local tangent projector, with the rest of the chain treated as fixed for that minibatch step.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this requires a sweep-style procedure where the center moves, the tangent basis is refreshed, and projection/rotation is recomputed as the update propagates through the chain.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The high-level paper language makes both methods sound like the same algorithmic idea, and the meeting is about diagnosing a bug rather than re-deriving the full execution plan, so neither expects the implementation granularity to be the point of disagreement.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'Adam baseline' they are comparing against
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the Adam baseline' as the comparison showing TSGO underperforming.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the Adam result recorded in the reproduction sheet from last week, produced before Marco's dataloader and loss-logging cleanup.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the latest tracked Adam run in the experiment system after the minibatch averaging fix, which has a different curve and endpoint.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There is only one socially salient Adam reference in each person's workflow, so the phrase feels uniquely identifying even though the lab currently has two plausible 'baseline' artifacts.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about whether the next patch would 'stabilize' or 'fix' training.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means eliminating obvious pathologies such as exploding norm, NaNs, or immediate oscillation in the first 2-3 epochs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means obtaining a smooth, reproducible 20-epoch likelihood trajectory that supports a fair claim that TSGO behaves better than Adam on the benchmark.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In troubleshooting meetings, 'stable' sounds like a shared engineering goal, but each person silently uses a different evidence threshold tied to their own responsibilities.
